1219.note: In the Landanger wine and grain merchant's journal and cash books (AD Haute-Marne 129 J 23, 35, 37), 'feuille volante chiffrée' most likely means a loose sheet of figures, not a cipher: the notice speaks of how the pages are filled ('Toutes les pages ne sont pas remplies de la même façon ... à la fin, présence d'une feuille volante chiffrée'), and the same fonds uses 'chiffre' for 'chiffre d'affaires'. Low confidence: no scan exists.
1219.access_note: AD Haute-Marne reading room; FranceArchives returns an empty JavaScript page to curl (16 Nov 2026).

seen.extent: One loose sheet at the end of a 400-page journal (129 J 23, 1931-34); five loose sheets in the cash book 129 J 35 (1909-13); 129 J 37 (1920-21).
seen.cipher: Archive description: 'Toutes les pages ne sont pas remplies de la même façon; à la fin, présence d'une feuille volante chiffrée' (129 J 23); '5 feuilles volantes chiffrées' (129 J 35). In an account book 'chiffrée' reads as 'covered with figures'.

1382.note: Not assessed: 'De inhoud van de telegrammen is veelal cryptisch' (ANRI Algemene Secretarie inv. 24, NA 2.10.14 inventory p. 74) may mean terse text with cover names or simply obscure wording; it does not say code groups exist, so neither open nor not_cipher can be shown. Blocker: held at ANRI Jakarta, unscanned. The ANRI microfilm inventory's code telegrams (Melbourne inv. 2012, Van Mook inv. 2043-2044) are better leads than inv. 24.

1215.note: Not assessed: AD Gard 74 J 38 (Gatimel autograph collection) lists one 'lettre chiffrée de la duchesse de Berry (1832)'. Her 1830-32 conspiracy correspondence is printed with decipherments in Bertier de Sauvigny, La conspiration des légitimistes et de la duchesse de Berry (1951), not reachable online, so this letter may already be read in print; a Chateaubriand appendix also reports her 1832 letters in sympathetic ink. Needs the AD Gard scan and Bertier de Sauvigny 1951.
1215.access_note: AD Gard reading room; Bertier de Sauvigny 1951 in print only.
